body:
I'm not able to reproduce (4.3-stable or 4.4.1-stable), but I might just not be following the steps to reproduce correctly. @BoydyBoydy if possible, could you help clarifying the reproduction steps a little? A video recording, screenshots for each step, and/or a zipped Minimal reproduction project to start from would be great!

The steps I'm unsure about is mostly these:
- What do I reparent the ColorRect to?
- What node are you calling 'background', is that the ColorRect?
- What Control should I delete?
- Where in the node hierarchy is the AnimationPlayer (if that matters)

When I delete a node that I have an animation for (and choose to not remove the tracks in the confirmation popup) it will look like the screenshot below ("background" is the deleted node), and nothing happens when I click the node name:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ffd1c33b-9968-48f3-ae35-eda670785c29)

cc @AThousandShips

Hi @Nallebeorn. I am double checking on 4.3 and 4.4.1

I have updated the process below. It has been a while since I have done this but I was able to get it working/erroring.
I still get the error for 4.3 but now do NOT get the error in 4.4.1 :)
Questions have been answered below, if needed.
Brief Results of testing for 4.3 and 4.4.1 are below.
If needed, I can attempt to get a reproduction project together, but when I reopened the project the problem was not there any more.

**Answered Questions**
- What do I reparent the ColorRect to?
Make this Scene Root
- What node are you calling 'background', is that the ColorRect?
yes, i meant 'to be renamed to', when I said called - i have left naming out of the process this time
- What Control should I delete?
there should only be the one Control generated when you start to create a User Interface - so the control that is now not the scene root
- Where in the node hierarchy is the AnimationPlayer (if that matters)
i do not think that this matters, but as a child under ColorRect
- Do you mean these Red 'x's (in screenshot)
yes those are the same 'x's that I get

**Redone Process:**
1. New Scene > User Interface
2. Add Child Node -> ColorRect, from Control
3. Add Child Node -> AnimationPlayer, from Control
4. Make ColorRect use Anchors and set to FullRect
5. Create a new Animation to fade out - changing the ColorRect Colour to something else
6. Add Track - Property Track for ColorRect/modulate
7. Create and update Key Frames from start and end, changing the end colour to something else
8. Make Scene Root - ColorRect -- Should see that control is now parent of AnimationPlayer
9. Move Animation Player as child node under ColorRect
10. Delete Control node
11. Clicking back on AnimationPlayer shows red 'x's
12. Within Animation - Single Click on ColorRect (the Node name above the properties with a White Node Circle)
13. CRASH / or it just closes

**4.3 Result**
Once reopened:
- animation does not show the red 'x's anymore
- animation has been erased
- ColorRect has reverted back to the original Gradient Rectangle icon

Not sure if below info is good
```
  scene/animation/animation_mixer.cpp:668 - AnimationMixer (at: animation-player-test.tscn): 'RESET', couldn't resolve track:  'Background:modulate'. This warning can be disabled in Project Settings. (User)
  scene/animation/animation_mixer.cpp:668 - AnimationMixer (at: animation-player-test.tscn): 'changeColour', couldn't resolve track:  'Background:modulate'. This warning can be disabled in Project Settings. (User)
```

As 4.3 is a previous version, I didn't copy out the output log

**4.4.1 - same process, but seems to not crash**

- Everything seems OK
- Red 'x's, but I assume that is due to not knowing where the original node is, as suggested in previous comment

Thank you, that's super clear! I can confirm the same behaviour following your new instructions, i.e. I can reproduce the crash in 4.3 but not 4.4.1.

This seems to be similar to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/91043, albeit with slightly different reproduction step, so it's possible this was also fixed by PR https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/94945 (just from reading the diff, that PR seems to also handle the case of the animation player's root node being null).

Thanks @Nallebeorn,
I agree that the similar case is probably the exact case required.
I had used the longer steps just in case because I couldn't identify the contributing factor/s. The simplified linked case gives what is needed.
So I think this is closed but I will leave that up to the team. Thanks for following up!
